layer1_identification.broadClassification: food prop / stylized low-poly game asset
layer1_identification.note: reference images are themselves stylized low-poly renders, not photographs; target look is faceted matte clay, same style family as pancake

layer2_form_silhouette.boundingVolume: flattened dome (squashed hemisphere) sitting on a flat base
layer2_form_silhouette.symmetry: radial about the vertical axis for the dome body; broken by the cross-slash which reads as two perpendicular linear cuts
layer2_form_silhouette.shapeLanguage: organic dome expressed with geometric faceting

measurements_px.front_elevation_width: ~1160 (edge to edge at widest, near the base)
measurements_px.front_elevation_width_over_height: 2.64 (a low, wide dome - flatter than a half-sphere, closer to the pancake stack's squashness but single-body)
measurements_px.topdown_ring_count: approximately 10-11 concentric rings visible from apex to about 85% of the radius
measurements_px.slash_reach_fraction_of_radius: cuts run from the very apex out to roughly 0.75-0.8 of the dome radius, stopping short of the base rim
measurements_px.slash_width_fraction_of_diameter: each cut arm is a narrow wedge, roughly 4-6% of the diameter wide at its widest (near center), tapering toward the tip

derivedRatios.widestPointHeight: at or very near the base (front elevation shows the silhouette is widest at the bottom edge, curving continuously up to the apex - a true dome, not a bulging equator like the pancake rim)

meso: cross-slash valley (two perpendicular cut lines meeting at the apex)
ear ridges (raised lip along each cut edge)
micro: concentric banneton ring grooves across the whole dome surface
flour dusting concentrated on ring ridges
darker-to-lighter radial color gradient across the dome

layer4_spatial: <cross-slash, embedded-in, dome body> contact: two perpendicular trenches cut into the dome surface, meeting at the apex, exposing a lighter crumb color at the floor
<ear ridge, adjoins, cross-slash edge> contact: a raised lip runs along each trench edge where the crust tore open
<ring grooves, embedded-in, dome body> contact: concentric shallow grooves, centered on the apex, covering the whole visible dome surface
no floating parts; single continuous body resting on a flat unseen base

layer5_materials.single_substance: opaque dielectric, matte crust + a second opaque dielectric, matte crumb (exposed at the slash)
layer5_materials.roughness: 1.0 (fully matte clay); no specular lobe anywhere
layer5_materials.relief: faceted planar shading; ring grooves read as shallow concentric channels, the slash reads as a deep V-trench with raised lip edges
layer5_materials.runtimeNote: consumer runtime force-replaces every material with MeshLambertMaterial keeping only map+color, so PBR scalars beyond albedo are inert (repo scripts/breads/types.ts section 2)

layer6_color.crustBase: #A9713F blending to a darker brown across the dome (gradient, no single hex given for the dark end - resolved deterministically, see author_spec.py)
layer6_color.crumbAtSlash: not specified in JSON hex - resolved as a warm golden interior tone consistent with the pancake precedent's 'rim exposes lighter tone' convention (see author_spec.py resolution note)
layer6_color.flourDusting: light, scattered unevenly, concentrated on the raised ring ridges

layer7_identity_features: spiral/concentric banneton ring markings pressed across the whole top surface - the single defining feature per assets/prompts/breads/campagne.json notes_ko
cross-shaped slash with raised burst ears along each cut line
uneven flour dusting on the ring ridges
layer8_uncertainty: underside is never visible in any of the three views or any turntable azimuth above the horizon - modelled as a flat closed base
exact ring phase/spiral pitch is not identity-critical; ring count and spacing are matched instead

the dark end of the crust gradient has no explicit hex in the prompt JSON; resolved by a documented deterministic darkening of the given #A9713F rather than by pixel sampling (banned by types.ts section 8)
crumb (interior) color at the slash has no explicit hex; resolved by the same documented method
